'''Emille Davie Lawrence''' is a [[mathematician]] specializing in [[topological graph theory]]. She is Term Associate Professor and Chair of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of San Francisco]].<ref name=":1" />

==Education and career==

Lawrence received her BS in Mathematics from [[Spelman College]]<ref name=":1" /> and her PhD in Mathematics from the [[University of Georgia]] in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Current and Former PhD Students {{!}} Department of Mathematics|url=https://www.math.uga.edu/current-and-former-phd-students|access-date=2021-04-08|website=www.math.uga.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Emille Davie - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=110350|access-date=2021-07-24|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> Her dissertation was jointly supervised by Clint McCrory and Will Kazez. She is a low-dimensional [[Topology|topologist]] with mathematical interests that include [[Braid group|braid groups]], [[geometric group theory]], and spatial [[Graphs and Combinatorics|graphs]]. She is also an advocate for broadening participation in the mathematical sciences through outreach and mentoring.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Chin|first=Steven|date=2015-06-29|title=Emille D. Lawrence|url=https://www.usfca.edu/faculty/emille-lawrence|access-date=2021-04-08|website=University of San Francisco|language=en}}</ref> She is Editor-In-Chief for the [[American Mathematical Society]]'s blog ''Math Mamas''.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-10-24|title=About the Editors|url=https://blogs.ams.org/mathmamas/about/|access-date=2021-07-24|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

In 2021, Lawrence received the [[AWM Service Award|Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) Service Award]] "for her service as Chair of the 50th Anniversary Committee and her leadership role as Chair, since 2016, of the Mentor Network Committee and for her mentorship as Founding Faculty Sponsor of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics|AWM]] Student Chapter at the University of San Francisco. In all of these roles, Emille has worked to increase participation in the AWM by a diverse population of mathematicians at all stages of their careers."<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title=Emille D. Lawrence Wins AWM Service Award|url=https://awm-math.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/AWM-News-NovDec-2020-PRINT.pdf|journal=AWM Newsletter}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=AWM Service Award 2021|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-service-award/awm-service-award-2021/}}</ref> 

In 2021, Lawrence was awarded a Karen Edge Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web|title=2021 Class of Karen EDGE Fellows|url=https://www.edgeforwomen.org/2021-class-of-karen-edge-fellows/}}</ref> and was featured on the AWM website ''Women Do Math''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emille Davie Lawrence|url=https://www.womendomath.org/emille-davie-lawrence/|website=Women Do Math|date=23 August 2017 }}</ref> In 2024, she was selected as a fellow of the Association for Women in Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web | title=2024 AWM Fellows |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) | date=2023-10-26 | url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2024-awm-fellows/ | ref={{sfnref | Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) | 2023}} | access-date=2024-08-10}}</ref>
